text: APIs, or Application Programming Interfaces, allow different software systems to communicate. When you work with an API, you typically send HTTP requests to a server, such as GET to fetch data or POST to send new information. The server usually responds with JSON, a lightweight format that is easy for both computers and humans to read. Before making requests, many APIs require authentication, often using an API key, to confirm your identity. Additionally, be mindful of rate limits, which restrict how many requests you can make in a certain period. Finally, always implement proper error handling to deal with issues like network problems or invalid responses without crashing your application.
